tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local replay derived from the prior C1-C7 abstract authority-gate contract. The slice models one protected effect accepted under active epoch E1, followed by loss of the acceptance response before the caller records success. It derives the minimum durable reconstruction fields and retry decision table needed for C5-C7 and falsifies one weak retry rule that blindly reissues the effect after timeout. No concrete provider, public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler mutation, hosted compute, richer-mode arbitration, finite quota, or second semantic leaf is tested.

initial_state.protected_surface_behavior: accept at most one logical effect for K within the guarded epoch/payload identity and durably expose the acceptance outcome

trace: Caller submits guarded effect {epoch:E1, key:K, payload:P1, attempt:A1}.
Protected surface atomically validates E1, accepts the logical effect for K, commits result R1, and durably records acceptance metadata.
The success response is lost before the caller records completion, so the caller observes timeout/unknown outcome.
A safe recovery path performs authoritative reconstruction before any new attempt: read current authority plus durable effect record keyed by K.
If the record proves committed under E1 with payload P1, recovery returns committed-duplicate/success-equivalent and does not create another effect.
If authority has advanced beyond E1 and no committed K record exists, the stale attempt is rejected and must not be replayed under the old epoch.

If the record is explicitly pending/in-progress, recovery preserves unknown/pending and defers a new effect until the authoritative record resolves across invocations; same-run waiting is unnecessary.

Only when authoritative reconstruction proves no committed/pending effect for K and the current authority still permits a fresh attempt may a new attempt identity be issued for the same logical key, subject to the same guarded acceptance rule.
minimum_durable_reconstruction_fields: authoritative_effect_status including committed, rejected, pending or absent
result identity or deterministic result reference when committed
current authority epoch/fence or a reference sufficient to prove whether the original epoch is still active

weak_retry_rule.rule: After any timeout, immediately submit a new attempt A2 for the same intended effect without first reading authoritative effect state.
falsification: In the modeled trace, A1 already committed but its response was lost.
Blind A2 cannot distinguish committed from absent. If deduplication is keyed only by attempt id, A2 is a distinct accepted request and can duplicate the protected effect.

Even if the surface rejects duplicates by K, blind retry still lacks evidence to classify committed, conflicting-payload, stale-epoch, or pending cases and therefore fails C6/C7 replay reconstruction.
Therefore timeout alone is not a safe retry predicate; authoritative reconstruction is required before retry.

observations: A lost acknowledgement converts a completed effect into a caller-side unknown outcome; retry safety therefore depends on durable authoritative effect evidence, not on transport timeout semantics.

An attempt identifier is insufficient as the sole idempotency key because a retry normally has a different attempt id; duplicate resistance must bind to a stable logical effect identity and stable payload/generation identity.

The reconstruction record must distinguish committed, conflicting committed, rejected-stale, pending and absent states; treating any read failure or timeout as absence reintroduces duplicate/conflict risk.
Cross-invocation checkpoint/resume is compatible with pending or unavailable reconstruction and avoids same-run polling without weakening duplicate resistance.
inference: For the exact abstract acknowledgement-loss model tested, C5-C7 require a stable logical effect key plus stable payload/generation identity and authoritative durable reconstruction before retry. Blind timeout reissue is falsified because it cannot distinguish an already-committed effect from absence and can duplicate the effect when deduplication is attempt-scoped. This narrows the minimum replay contract without claiming any concrete Chat-exposed provider satisfies it.
